cards.topic: 24.11. Pledge I — Function, types, securities
cards.front: What problem does the right of pledge solve (example Labrax/Philto)?
cards.back:
Labrax lends Philto 100 without security; Philto becomes insolvent and the creditors share his assets pro rata → Labrax receives only 30.
• With a pledge (eg a piece from Philto's art collection) he could have had the pledge auctioned once the debt fell due (after obtaining it by an action in rem) and satisfied himself from the proceeds — even in bankruptcy: separation of the pledge from the bankruptcy assets.
cards.old_front: Welches Problem löst das Pfandrecht (Beispiel Labrax/Philto)?

cards.topic: 24.11. Pledge I — Function, types, securities
cards.front: What does the right of pledge grant the creditor — where does its advantage lie?
cards.back:
A right in another's thing: if the debtor does not pay when the debt falls due, the creditor may enforce the pledge (usually by public auction) and satisfy himself from the proceeds.
• Advantage above all in bankruptcy: instead of a mere quota, separation of the pledge and full satisfaction, as far as the proceeds suffice.
cards.old_front: Was gewährt das Pfandrecht dem Gläubiger — worin liegt sein Vorteil?

cards.topic: 24.11. Pledge I — Function, types, securities
cards.front: Which types of rights of pledge exist by origin and by possession?
cards.back:
By origin: contractual, judicial, statutory right of pledge.
By possession: possessory pledge (the thing is delivered to the creditor) vs non-possessory pledge (hypothec/lien — the pledger keeps the thing).
cards.old_front: Welche Arten von Pfandrechten gibt es nach Entstehung und nach Besitz?

cards.topic: 24.11. Pledge I — Function, types, securities
cards.front: Possessory vs non-possessory pledge — advantages and disadvantages?
cards.back:
Possessory pledge: added security (the thing is already with the creditor when the debt falls due) and publicity of the disposition.
Non-possessory pledge: the pledger can continue to use the thing and so earn the capital needed for repayment.
• The possessory pledgee has NATURAL possession (for the pledger, who remains proprietary possessor), but interdict protection.
cards.old_front: Besitzpfand vs besitzloses Pfand — Vor- und Nachteile?

cards.topic: 24.11. Pledge I — Function, types, securities
cards.front: Which other securities does Roman law know (FIDEIUSSIO, FIDUCIA CUM CREDITORE)?
cards.back:
FIDEIUSSIO (personal guarantee): the guarantor promises to pay the debt → only a personal claim against him (no right in rem); he is liable with all his assets; the creditor chooses whom to sue.
FIDUCIA CUM CREDITORE (transfer of ownership by way of security, early Roman): ownership of a thing of the debtor passes to the creditor; if the debtor pays, it must be reconveyed — ACTIO FIDUCIAE DIRECTA (debtor) / CONTRARIA (creditor).
• FIDUCIA = trust: externally the fiduciary can do more than he is internally permitted to.
cards.old_front: Welche anderen Sicherungsmittel kennt das römische Recht (FIDEIUSSIO, FIDUCIA CUM CREDITORE)?

cards.topic: 24.11. Pledge I — Function, types, securities
cards.front: Pledge by the debtor vs third-party pledge vs personal guarantee — what extends the assets available to the creditor?
cards.back:
Pledge by the debtor: no extension of the assets available, but a preferential right in the pledged thing.
Third-party pledge: a third party's thing is liable in addition to the debtor's assets — the third party is liable only with that thing.
Personal guarantee: the guarantor's entire assets are liable in addition.
cards.old_front: Pfand des Schuldners vs Drittpfand vs Bürgschaft — was erweitert die Haftungsmasse?

cards.topic: 24.11. Pledge I — Pledge as a right in rem and the contract of pledge
cards.front: What are the three meanings of the word PIGNUS?
cards.back:
1. The pledged thing itself.
2. The creditor's right of pledge in rem over the thing.
3. The real contract between pledger and pledgee (contract of pledge).
cards.old_front: Welche drei Bedeutungen hat das Wort PIGNUS?

cards.topic: 24.11. Pledge I — Pledge as a right in rem and the contract of pledge
cards.front: Right of pledge (in rem) vs contract of pledge — how does each arise?
cards.back:
Right of pledge: by pledge agreement (CONVENTIO PIGNORIS) — delivery not required.
Contract of pledge: real contract, arises only upon delivery of the pledged thing (with a non-possessory pledge, therefore only once the creditor obtains possession, eg by VINDICATIO PIGNORIS).
cards.old_front: Pfandrecht (dinglich) vs Pfandvertrag — wie entsteht was?

cards.topic: 24.11. Pledge I — Pledge as a right in rem and the contract of pledge
cards.front: What are the three requirements of the right of pledge as a right in rem?
cards.back:
a. A monetary claim to be secured (accessoriality — no valid claim, no right of pledge).
b. Ownership (bonitarian suffices) or power of disposal of the pledger (NEMO PLUS IURIS …).
c. CONVENTIO PIGNORIS — agreement that the thing secures the claim (a disposition under property law; determines which things secure which debts).
• Klausur formula: pledger's power of disposal + pledge agreement + claim to be secured.
cards.old_front: Welche drei Voraussetzungen hat das Pfandrecht als dingliches Recht?

cards.topic: 24.11. Pledge I — Pledge as a right in rem and the contract of pledge
cards.front: What does the “accessoriality” of the right of pledge mean?
cards.back:
The creation and continued existence of the right of pledge depend on the secured claim: no claim, no right of pledge; if the claim terminates, the pledge terminates.
• Debtor and pledger can be different persons (third-party pledge).
cards.old_front: Was bedeutet „Akzessorietät“ des Pfandrechts?

cards.topic: 24.11. Pledge I — Pledge as a right in rem and the contract of pledge
cards.front: Must the pledger be the owner? What applies if he becomes owner later?
cards.back:
He needs ownership (bonitarian suffices) or power of disposal — otherwise no valid right of pledge (NEMO PLUS IURIS …).
• If he later acquires ownership (eg by inheritance), the creditor's position is cured (convalescence) → ACTIO PIGNERATICIA (IN REM) UTILIS.
cards.old_front: Muss der Verpfänder Eigentümer sein? Was gilt, wenn er es später wird?

cards.topic: 24.11. Pledge I — Pledge as a right in rem and the contract of pledge
cards.front: Which action in rem does the pledgee have — against whom, with what result?
cards.back:
ACTIO PIGNERATICIA IN REM = VINDICATIO PIGNORIS (sources also: ACTIO SERVIANA, QUASI SERVIANA, HYPOTHECARIA).
• At the latest from maturity and non-payment, against any possessor — including the pledger; likewise if the possessory pledge has been lost.
• As with the REI VINDICATIO, condemnation in money (if the thing is not restored): the debtor only up to the amount of the debt; other possessors to the full value — the creditor keeps the amount of the debt and gives the surplus (SUPERFLUUM) to the pledger.
cards.old_front: Welche dingliche Klage hat der Pfandgläubiger — gegen wen, mit welchem Ergebnis?

cards.topic: 24.11. Pledge I — Pledge as a right in rem and the contract of pledge
cards.front: How does the possessory pledgee defend himself against the pledger's REI VINDICATIO? What is the INTERDICTUM SALVIANUM?
cards.back:
EXCEPTIO PIGNERATICIA.
INTERDICTUM SALVIANUM: if a lessee has expressly pledged the movables brought onto the leasehold (INVECTA ILLATA) to the lessor, the lessor uses it to obtain possession of them for the first time.
cards.old_front: Wie wehrt sich der Besitzpfandgläubiger gegen die REI VINDICATIO des Verpfänders? Was ist das INTERDICTUM SALVIANUM?

cards.topic: 24.11. Pledge I — Pledge as a right in rem and the contract of pledge
cards.front: What can the pledger claim under the contract of pledge (ACTIO PIGNERATICIA IN PERSONAM DIRECTA)?
cards.back:
Return of the pledged thing as soon as a requirement of the right of pledge ceases to exist (debt paid — accessoriality; waiver by the creditor, eg by permission to alienate).
• After enforcement, the surplus proceeds (SUPERFLUUM, HYPEROCHA).
• Once the debt has terminated, even the return of another's thing that he pledged without the owner's consent (Ulpian D 13.7.9.4, Case 161a).
cards.old_front: Was kann der Verpfänder aus dem Pfandvertrag verlangen (ACTIO PIGNERATICIA IN PERSONAM DIRECTA)?

cards.topic: 24.11. Pledge I — Pledge as a right in rem and the contract of pledge
cards.front: What can the pledgee claim under the contract of pledge (ACTIO PIGNERATICIA IN PERSONAM CONTRARIA)?
cards.back:
Compensation for damage the pledged thing has caused him and for expenses incurred on it.
• Eg Lucius/Omphale: a sick cow is pledged, Omphale's calf is infected and dies → compensation for the calf and the vet.
• Also if the pledger delivered a thing without procuring a right of pledge (another's thing): claim to the creation of a valid right of pledge (Ulpian D 13.7.9 pr, Case 161a).
cards.old_front: Was kann der Pfandgläubiger aus dem Pfandvertrag verlangen (ACTIO PIGNERATICIA IN PERSONAM CONTRARIA)?

cards.topic: 24.11. Pledge I — Pledge as a right in rem and the contract of pledge
cards.front: Why does a SUPERFLUUM often arise?
cards.back: Because the creditor usually demands a security whose value clearly exceeds the debt (protection against falling prices) → the proceeds often exceed the claim; the remainder is due to the pledger (or to junior creditors).
cards.old_front: Warum entsteht oft ein SUPERFLUUM?

cards.topic: 24.11. Pledge I — Alienation, enforcement, pledging another's thing, termination
cards.front: What applies if the pledger alienates the pledged thing WITH the creditor's consent?
cards.back:
a. Consent without reservation = waiver of the right of pledge → it terminates upon alienation; the buyer acquires unburdened ownership (Marcianus D 20.6.8.14, 8.15).
b. Consent with the right of pledge reserved → the buyer acquires ownership burdened with the right of pledge (NEMO PLUS IURIS …).
• The secured claim continues to exist in both cases.
cards.old_front: Was gilt, wenn der Verpfänder die Pfandsache MIT Zustimmung des Gläubigers veräußert?

cards.topic: 24.11. Pledge I — Alienation, enforcement, pledging another's thing, termination
cards.front: What applies if the pledger alienates the pledged thing WITHOUT the creditor's consent?
cards.back:
Not permitted in principle; the consequences are disputed:
a. Movable thing, knowingly: the pledger is a FUR (Paulus (Iulianus) D 47.2.67 pr, Case 164) → liable to the creditor; the buyer probably acquires no ownership, only possession (the pledger remains owner).
b. No FURTUM (pledger in good faith, or land): the buyer probably acquires ownership, burdened with the right of pledge.
• In both cases the right of pledge continues → VINDICATIO PIGNORIS against any possessor. It ends only when the thing ceases to exist (also by SPECIFICATIO).
cards.old_front: Was gilt, wenn der Verpfänder die Pfandsache OHNE Zustimmung des Gläubigers veräußert?

cards.topic: 24.11. Pledge I — Alienation, enforcement, pledging another's thing, termination
cards.front: How is a pledge enforced? What are the PACTUM DE VENDENDO and the LEX COMMISSORIA?
cards.back:
Upon non-payment the creditor sells the thing (usually by public auction) and satisfies himself from the proceeds; the right of pledge authorises him to transfer the pledger's ownership (Ulpian D 13.7.4, Case 169). If the proceeds are insufficient, the remaining claim persists.
• Late classical: tacit right of sale (PACTUM DE VENDENDO/DISTRAHENDO).
• LEX COMMISSORIA (forfeiture clause: on non-payment the creditor becomes owner) fell out of use because it enriched the creditor without justification; Constantine prohibited it in 320 AD (cf § 1371 ABGB, § 1229 BGB, Art 894 ZGB).
• Prior notice (DENUNTIATIO) required — post-classical: three times.
cards.old_front: Wie wird ein Pfand verwertet? Was sind PACTUM DE VENDENDO und LEX COMMISSORIA?

cards.topic: 24.11. Pledge I — Alienation, enforcement, pledging another's thing, termination
cards.front: After enforcement of the pledge — what applies to the other rights of pledge and to the settlement of accounts?
cards.back:
• All rights of pledge in the thing terminate; junior creditors claim their share of the SUPERFLUUM with an ACTIO UTILIS.
• If several things are pledged, the creditor chooses which one to sell (Modestinus D 20.5.8).
• Settlement: pledger → ACTIO PIGNERATICIA IN PERSONAM DIRECTA (surplus proceeds); creditor → ACTIO PIGNERATICIA IN PERSONAM CONTRARIA (expenses, damage).
cards.old_front: Was gilt nach der Pfandverwertung für die übrigen Pfandrechte und die Abrechnung?

cards.topic: 24.11. Pledge I — Alienation, enforcement, pledging another's thing, termination
cards.front: Paulus D 13.7.41 (Case 161), 1st case: T pledges another's thing to C without authority and later acquires ownership of it himself. Legal situation?
cards.back:
Convalescence: T's acquisition of ownership retroactively cures C's right of pledge → C has a right in rem, enforceable with the ACTIO PIGNERATICIA (IN REM) UTILIS.
• The direct action does not fit, because its formula requires the pledger's ownership at the time of pledging.
cards.old_front: Paulus D 13.7.41 (Case 161), 1. Fall: T verpfändet unbefugt eine fremde Sache an C und erwirbt später selbst das Eigentum daran. Rechtslage?

cards.topic: 24.11. Pledge I — Alienation, enforcement, pledging another's thing, termination
cards.front: Controversy Paulus D 13.7.41 (Case 161, 2nd case) vs Modestinus D 20.1.22 (Case 160): Titius pledges E's thing to his creditor C without authority, dies, and E becomes his heir. Does the right of pledge convalesce?
cards.back:
Paulus: No — E never intended to create a right of pledge; it is unacceptable that his ownership be burdened merely because of the succession (owner's private autonomy).
Modestinus: Yes — cured, C has the ACTIO PIGNERATICIA (IN REM) UTILIS (creditor's need for protection; E inherits the estate and succeeds to the debt, including the obligation to create the pledge).
• Difference from case 1: there the pledger himself acquires ownership; here the owner steps into the pledger's position.
• Also listed in the exam materials as an important controversy.
cards.old_front: Kontroverse Paulus D 13.7.41 (Case 161, 2. Fall) vs Modestinus D 20.1.22 (Case 160): Titius verpfändet unbefugt eine Sache des E an seinen Gläubiger C, stirbt, und E wird sein Erbe. Konvalesziert das Pfandrecht?

cards.topic: 24.11. Pledge I — Alienation, enforcement, pledging another's thing, termination
cards.front: On which grounds does the right of pledge terminate before enforcement?
cards.back:
1. Termination of the claim (payment, release, set-off) — accessoriality.
2. Waiver by the creditor (also by unreserved permission to alienate).
3. The creditor becomes owner of the pledged thing (CONFUSIO — no pledge in one's own thing).
4. The thing ceases to exist — destruction or (irreversible) SPECIFICATIO.
• Not by USUCAPIO of a third party (Papinian D 41.3.44.5: NON MUTAT USUCAPIO SUPERVENIENS … QUO MINUS PIGNORIS PERSECUTIO SALVA SIT).
cards.old_front: Aus welchen Gründen erlischt das Pfandrecht vor der Verwertung?

cards.topic: 24.11. Pledge I — Alienation, enforcement, pledging another's thing, termination
cards.front: What does INDIVISA EST PIGNORIS CAUSA mean?
cards.back: Principle of indivisible liability of the pledge: if several things are pledged, each is liable for the entire claim as long as even part of the debt remains (Papinian D 21.2.65; Ulpian D 20.1.19, Case 166).
cards.old_front: Was bedeutet INDIVISA EST PIGNORIS CAUSA?

cards.topic: 24.11. Pledge I — Alienation, enforcement, pledging another's thing, termination
cards.front: Marcianus D 20.6.8.14 (Case 162): the pledgee permits a sale for 10; the pledger sells for 5. Has the creditor waived the pledge?
cards.back:
No — the pledger has breached the agreement (minimum price) → no waiver; the creditor can bring the VINDICATIO PIGNORIS against the buyer.
• If he sells for more than 10, the permission is a waiver → the buyer acquires unburdened ownership.
cards.old_front: Marcianus D 20.6.8.14 (Case 162): Der Pfandgläubiger erlaubt den Verkauf um 10; der Verpfänder verkauft um 5. Hat der Gläubiger auf das Pfand verzichtet?

cards.topic: 24.11. Pledge I — Alienation, enforcement, pledging another's thing, termination
cards.front: Paulus D 20.1.29.2 (Case 170): A pledges his house to B and C; it burns down. Lucius Titius buys the land without knowing of the pledge and builds a new house. Legal situation?
cards.back:
• House and land form a unit (SUPERFICIES SOLO CEDIT) — one can only pledge both. After the fire the pledge continues in the land (loss of value, not destruction).
• The new house becomes part of the pledged thing again → B and C can claim house and land from Lucius Titius with the VINDICATIO PIGNORIS.
• Lucius Titius (bona fide builder): EXCEPTIO DOLI → retention until his building costs are reimbursed, insofar as they have actually increased the value.
• Model exegesis in the textbook (ch. XV.E).
cards.old_front: Paulus D 20.1.29.2 (Case 170): A verpfändet sein Haus an B und C; es brennt ab. Lucius Titius kauft das Grundstück, ohne vom Pfand zu wissen, und baut ein neues Haus. Rechtslage?

cards.topic: 24.11. Pledge I — Alienation, enforcement, pledging another's thing, termination
cards.front: Paulus (Cassius) D 13.7.18.3 (Case 170a): D pledges his forest to E; a ship is built from the timber. Does E have a right of pledge in the ship?
cards.back:
No (Cassius): timber or forest and ship are physically different (ALIUD) — shipbuilding as SPECIFICATIO (NOVA SPECIES); when the pledged object ceases to exist, the right of pledge terminates.
• The interpretation of the pledge agreement is decisive: had the forest been pledged “and everything made from it or growing on it”, the pledge would cover the ship — unless a third party does the processing and acquires ownership originally.
cards.old_front: Paulus (Cassius) D 13.7.18.3 (Case 170a): D verpfändet seinen Wald an E; aus dem Holz wird ein Schiff gebaut. Hat E ein Pfandrecht am Schiff?

cards.topic: 24.11. Pledge I — Textbook exercises (Ex 53–56)
cards.front: [Textbook Ex 53a] On 1 March Victor delivers a silver table to Iris as a pledge for a debt of Rufus. On 1 September Iris learns that the table belongs to Laura, who knows nothing of this. Legal situation — can Iris take action against Victor?
cards.back:
• Third-party pledge: pledger Victor ≠ debtor Rufus. Victor is neither owner nor authorised to dispose → no valid right of pledge (NEMO PLUS IURIS …). Iris has only natural possession.
• But the real contract (contract of pledge) came into existence upon delivery → with the ACTIO PIGNERATICIA IN PERSONAM CONTRARIA Iris can demand that Victor procure a valid right of pledge (Ulpian D 13.7.9 pr) — economically worth only as much as Victor's assets.
• Laura remains owner → REI VINDICATIO against Iris.
cards.old_front: [Lehrbuch Ex 53a] Victor übergibt Iris am 1.3. einen Silbertisch als Pfand für eine Schuld des Rufus. Am 1.9. erfährt Iris, dass der Tisch Laura gehört, die nichts weiß. Rechtslage — kann Iris gegen Victor vorgehen?

cards.topic: 24.11. Pledge I — Textbook exercises (Ex 53–56)
cards.front: [Textbook Ex 53b] Victor has delivered Laura's silver table to Iris as a pledge for Rufus' debt. What applies if Iris' claim already terminates on 1 July?
cards.back:
• With the claim, every basis for the pledge falls away (accessoriality) — including the claim to the creation of a pledge.
• Victor can reclaim the table with the ACTIO PIGNERATICIA IN PERSONAM DIRECTA, although it does not belong to him (Ulpian D 13.7.9.4).
• (Not with the REI VINDICATIO — he is not the owner; Laura can vindicate.)
cards.old_front: [Lehrbuch Ex 53b] Victor hat Iris Lauras Silbertisch als Pfand für Rufus' Schuld übergeben. Was gilt, wenn Iris' Forderung schon am 1.7. erlischt?

cards.topic: 24.11. Pledge I — Textbook exercises (Ex 53–56)
cards.front: [Textbook Ex 54] Aurelia grants her creditor Daphne a non-possessory pledge in a cart (debt 1.700) that she believes to be hers; it belongs to her brother Carus. Carus dies, Aurelia is sole heir. (a) Can Daphne demand that the cart be handed over? (b) What if instead Aurelia dies and Carus is her heir?
cards.back:
(a) Yes — convalescence: the pledger herself becomes owner (as in Paulus D 13.7.41, 1st case) → Daphne has a right of pledge and the ACTIO PIGNERATICIA (IN REM) UTILIS; enforcement, SUPERFLUUM to Aurelia.
(b) Disputed: Paulus (D 13.7.41, 2nd case) — no convalescence, Carus never wanted to pledge; Modestinus (D 20.1.22) — cured, because the owner steps into the pledger's position (and into her debt).
cards.old_front: [Lehrbuch Ex 54] Aurelia bestellt ihrer Gläubigerin Daphne ein besitzloses Pfand an einem Wagen (Schuld 1.700), den sie für ihren hält; er gehört ihrem Bruder Carus. Carus stirbt, Aurelia ist Alleinerbin. (a) Kann Daphne den Wagen herausverlangen? (b) Was, wenn stattdessen Aurelia stirbt und Carus sie beerbt?

cards.topic: 24.11. Pledge I — Textbook exercises (Ex 53–56)
cards.front: [Textbook Ex 55] Flora grants Gripus a non-possessory pledge in her cow and then sells and delivers the cow to Hermes without informing Gripus. (a) Legal situation? (b) Difference if Gripus consents to the sale?
cards.back:
(a) Knowing alienation of a movable pledged thing without consent → Flora is a FUR (D 47.2.67 pr): ACTIO FURTI for Gripus. Hermes probably acquires no ownership, only possession; usucaption fails because the thing is stolen. Gripus' right of pledge continues → VINDICATIO PIGNORIS against Hermes.
(b) Unreserved consent = waiver → Hermes acquires unburdened ownership; the claim remains. Consent with the pledge reserved → Hermes acquires burdened ownership.
cards.old_front: [Lehrbuch Ex 55] Flora bestellt Gripus ein besitzloses Pfand an ihrer Kuh und verkauft und übergibt die Kuh dann an Hermes, ohne Gripus zu informieren. (a) Rechtslage? (b) Unterschied, wenn Gripus dem Verkauf zustimmt?

cards.topic: 24.11. Pledge I — Textbook exercises (Ex 53–56)
cards.front: [Textbook Ex 56] Niobe lends Brontes 1.000 for one year; Brontes pledges and delivers his team of oxen (Castor and Pollux, 600 each). (a) Shortly before maturity Niobe returns the oxen so that Brontes can sell them to Ago for 1.400; he gambles away the proceeds. (b) Brontes repays 700 and demands one ox back. (c) Both oxen die a natural death while with Niobe.
cards.back:
(a) Return for an unreserved sale = waiver → Ago acquires unburdened ownership; Niobe is left only with the unsecured claim for 1.000.
(b) No — INDIVISA EST PIGNORIS CAUSA: both oxen are liable until the whole debt (remaining 300) is paid; Niobe need not hand over either (she may do so as a courtesy).
(c) When the pledged things cease to exist, the right of pledge terminates; the claim remains. Niobe is not liable (no fault).
cards.old_front: [Lehrbuch Ex 56] Niobe leiht Brontes 1.000 für ein Jahr; Brontes verpfändet und übergibt sein Ochsengespann (Castor und Pollux, je 600). (a) Kurz vor Fälligkeit gibt Niobe die Ochsen zurück, damit Brontes sie an Ago um 1.400 verkauft; er verspielt den Erlös. (b) Brontes zahlt 700 zurück und verlangt einen Ochsen heraus. (c) Beide Ochsen sterben bei Niobe eines natürlichen Todes.
